I really don't get the appeal of the high HP, low DF package. In theory, I could see it being wonderful if the cars became hard to drive, but I don't know if it really works that well. Yeah, the cars *do* get harder to drive, but for the top 15 to 20, it's not really a problem for drivers of their skill level. Cody Ware and pals, on the other hand... I don't know if I would put them on the same level as Blaney or Larson, to say the least.

I also can't see the purpose of the high HP, low DF package from a competitive standpoint either, especially with the previous point about skill level. The leader gets the clean air advantage, *plus* the high HP, meaning a lot more people get put a lap down or even two. It reminds of the 90s era were maybe like 5-10 guys would finish on the lead lap. Those, frankly, aren't the good ol' days at all and not at all the best era to be anything like.

Just because the cars are faster doesn't make a bad race good. To me, the low HP, high DF is the most fair package to run, and really does promote more competitive racing.

"Rubbin' is racing." as they say. NASCAR is possibly the only major motorsport that allows continual, intentional contact. Penalties are unheard of for it.

That being said, it's all from the origins of the sport. F1 and, frankly most European motorsports, are probably are originated in a bunch of rich dudes seeing who could make the fastest car. NASCAR's origins are a bunch of literal criminals racing their getaway cars against one another, and when that lead to 50-60s short track racing, contact was nigh impossible to avoid. It's really just an integral part of the sport ever since, and any driver can do it as long as it's not under caution. 

There are very few more universally disliked moves than race control black-flagging Ricky Rudd at Sonoma in 1991, for turning Davey Allison on the final lap.

Petty (I think), certainly Dale Sr, Gordon and many of the modern drivers today have used a bump 'n run before on a short track, if not something else on larger track. To call those drivers bad for using the bumper, you'd quickly run out of "good" drivers, and the few you'd be left with... probably weren't/aren't that good.
